LESSON: TAQWA

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Pillars of Iman
Topic 3.2: Taqwa

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Taqwa. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What actions lead to piety?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the qualities of a pious person (Muttaqiin) for character building
2. demonstrate consciousness of Allah (S.W.T.) as a mark of true belief
3. appreciate the virtue of taqwa as a pre-condition for success in this life and the Hereafter

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: TAQWA
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Taqwa helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: TAQWA
Study Taqwa like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the qualities of a pious person (Muttaqiin) for character building

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the qualities of a pious person (Muttaqiin) for character building. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the qualities of a pious person (Muttaqiin) for character building.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Taqwa” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the qualities of a pious person (Muttaqiin) for character building. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Demonstrate consciousness of Allah (S.W.T.) as a mark of true belief

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate consciousness of Allah (S.W.T.) as a mark of true belief. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate consciousness of Allah (S.W.T.) as a mark of true belief.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Taqwa in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate consciousness of Allah (S.W.T.) as a mark of true belief. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the virtue of taqwa as a pre-condition for success in this life and the Hereafter

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the virtue of taqwa as a pre-condition for success in this life and the Hereafter. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the virtue of taqwa as a pre-condition for success in this life and the Hereafter.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the virtue of taqwa as a pre-condition for success in this life and the Hereafter. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Taqwa is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Taqwa” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify the qualities of a pious person (Muttaqiin) for character building)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Taqwa in your own words. (skill: demonstrate consciousness of Allah (S.W.T.) as a mark of true belief)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate the virtue of taqwa as a pre-condition for success in this life and the Hereafter)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Taqwa to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the qualities of a pious person (Muttaqiin) for character building.
3. Practise this skill: demonstrate consciousness of Allah (S.W.T.) as a mark of true belief.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the virtue of taqwa as a pre-condition for success in this life and the Hereafter.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Taqwa from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Taqwa: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Taqwa?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What actions lead to piety?
2. Why is taqwa important in the life of a Muslim?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Taqwa means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the qualities of a pious person (Muttaqiin) for character building.
5. Be able to: demonstrate consciousness of Allah (S.W.T.) as a mark of true belief.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
